title: Sell Mineral Rights in Parrish, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Parrish, AL | Walker County Coal
metaDescription: Family land near Parrish, AL tied to old Walker County coal camps? Get a title-checked mineral rights offer, no pressure and no obligation.
heroLead: Parrish grew up as a cluster of coal camps along the old rail lines of Walker County, and the mineral title behind the town still reflects how many small companies once worked these same coal seams before consolidating or folding entirely.
intro: Small coal camps like the ones that became Parrish were often worked by companies that existed for a decade or two, sold their leases to a competitor, and disappeared from the record. That churn makes tracing a Parrish-area mineral interest back to its origin more of a chain-of-title project than a simple deed lookup, especially for interests that were leased for CBM decades after the original coal company was gone.

sections.heading: Tracing an Interest Through Several Coal Companies
paragraphs: It's common for a Parrish-area tract to have passed through two or three coal or land companies before landing with whoever holds it today, and each transfer should have been recorded at the Walker County Courthouse in Jasper even if the company itself no longer exists. We build that chain ourselves rather than asking a family to track down defunct corporate records.

sections.heading: Old Camp Boundaries and Modern Parcel Lines
paragraphs: Because the original coal camp boundaries didn't always line up neatly with how land is platted today, some Parrish-area legal descriptions reference old camp names or survey markers that take extra work to match to current parcels. That's routine for us, and it's part of why we verify title ourselves before quoting a number rather than relying on what a family believes they own.

faqs.question: The coal company that originally owned our family's land folded decades ago. Can you still buy the interest?
faqs.answer: Yes. We trace how the interest was sold or transferred after the company folded — that's standard chain-of-title work for us in this part of Walker County.

faqs.question: Our deed references an old coal camp name we don't recognize on current maps.
faqs.answer: That's common around Parrish. We match old survey references to current parcels as part of confirming title before we make an offer.

faqs.question: Is our interest coal, methane, or both?
faqs.answer: It depends on what was reserved in the original conveyance. We check the record and tell you plainly what your family actually holds.

faqs.question: How long does chain-of-title research like this usually take?
faqs.answer: Most Parrish-area tracts take a few days to a couple of weeks to fully trace, depending on how many transfers are involved. We keep you posted as we work through it.
